selectedReaderNotes.text: The image is of fixing the movable bridges of a zither so that it can no longer be tuned: a figure for rigidly applying a rule.

We haven’t read these unofficial tales and don’t know the full story, but surely we’ve seen the two plays? A child of three knows them, let alone us!’

selectedReaderNotes.title: The child in motley
selectedReaderNotes.text: The allusion is to an exemplary filial son entertaining his aged parents in brightly patterned children’s clothes. Xi-feng turns the example into a playful defence of making the old lady laugh.

anchor.text: ‘These last few years, since we became related by marriage, haven’t I learnt any number of rules of behaviour? Even if we hadn’t grown up as brother and sister, even if we only reckoned him a brother-in-law, there’s still the “motley-clad child at play” in the Twenty-four Examples of Filial Piety. If they can’t come and play the child to make Grandmother laugh, and I’ve finally managed to coax a laugh out of her and get her to eat a little more, surely everyone’s pleased. They ought to thank me. Would they turn round and laugh at me instead?’

selectedReaderNotes.text: Tan-chun is formally reckoned as the principal wife’s daughter, although Aunt Zhao is her birth mother. Her claim about her uncle follows that distinction.
